title: Bulk Ising superconductivity in an intercalated TaSe2 bilayer structure
authors: Yupeng Li, Zhaopeng Guo, Lihong Hu, Guoan Li, Siqi Wu, Xinyi Zheng, Xiao Deng, Zhiyuan Zhang, Anqi Wang, Xingchen Guo, Ziwei Dou, Peiling Li, Yuke Li, Fanming Qu, Guangtong Liu, Jin-Ke Bao, Guang-Han Cao, Li Lu, Jie Shen, Zhu-An Xu
abstract: Ising spin-orbit coupling in bulk systems has drawn considerable interest for its ability to conveniently construct spin-orbit environments and enable exotic quantum phenomena. In this work, we synthesize intercalated 2Hb-TaSe$_2$ bilayers with noncentrosymmetric structure and, through multifaceted analysis, present multiple lines of evidence for the emergence of bulk Ising superconductivity. Resistivity measurements reveal anisotropic superconducting behavior, with a remarkably large in-plane upper critical field $B_{c2}^{\|}$ that exceeds the Pauli limit $B_{p}$. Band structure calculations further show band splitting accompanied by out-of-plane spin polarization. Collectively, these observations point to the presence of Ising superconductivity. Additional measurements of the thickness-dependent ratio $B_{c2}^{\|}$/$B_{p}$ and the superconducting diode effect not only further support the Ising superconducting nature of this material, but also reveal additional features of bulk Ising superconductivity evolving with thickness. Our findings provide valuable insights that may contribute to the search for bulk Ising superconductors.
summary: The study reports on bulk and thin-film superconductors based on intercalated $	ext{TaSe}_2$ bilayers. By measuring anisotropic critical fields and observing a persistent Superconducting Diode Effect, the authors provide strong evidence that Ising Spin-Orbit Coupling is the key mechanism driving their unconventional superconductivity. This research advances the search for materials exhibiting robust, high-field superconducting states.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of bulk Ising superconductivity (IS) in intercalated TaSe2 bilayers, specifically aiming to explain an exceptionally large upper critical field ($B_{c2}$) exceeding the Pauli limit.
main_result: Multiple experimental and theoretical analyses strongly support that the observed superconducting behavior is governed by Ising Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC), which manifests as anisotropic $B_{c2}$ and a persistent Superconducting Diode Effect (SDE).
method: The research combines synthesis of noncentrosymmetric bilayers, transport measurements ($R$-$T$, $B$-field sweeps), theoretical band structure calculations (DFT), and fitting to advanced superconducting models (AGL, Tinkham).
model_or_system: The physical system is the intercalated $	ext{InBr}(	ext{TaSe}_2)_2$ bilayer, which possesses a noncentrosymmetric rhombohedral crystal structure. The superconductivity is analyzed across bulk and thin-film limits.
key_observables: Anisotropic upper critical fields ($B_{\parallel}c_2$, $B_{\perp}c_2$), the ratio $B_{\parallel}c_2/B_p$ (observed to be large, e.g., $\sim 3.56$), and the Superconducting Diode Effect ($\Delta I_c$).
important_parameters: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c = 2.26 	ext{ K}$), Pauli limit ($B_p$), and thickness dependence of superconducting parameters.
main_assumptions: The authors attribute the large $B_{\parallel}c_2/B_p$ ratio and SDE primarily to Ising SOC, ruling out other mechanisms like Superconducting Orbital Screening (SOS) or Meissner screening as the sole cause.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structure confirmation (HRTEM/SXRD), anisotropic superconducting behavior via $B_{c2}$ vs. field plots, thickness dependence of $T_c$ and $B_{\parallel}c_2/B_p$, and mapping of the Superconducting Diode Effect ($\Delta I_c$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing bulk superconductivity and its anisotropy, then using thickness-dependent measurements and SDE analysis to distinguish between competing pairing mechanisms (Ising SOC vs. SOS), culminating in a comprehensive conclusion favoring Ising SOC.
why_interesting: This work provides experimental evidence for realizing and characterizing exotic superconducting states driven by strong spin-orbit coupling in layered materials, which is highly relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity mechanisms beyond BCS theory.
